Few things compare to seeing the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in person on a crisp November morning. Watching massive balloons float down the streets of New York City is an iconic holiday experience on many families’ travel wish lists.

Assuming you don’t live near the Big Apple, seeing the parade may require forgoing (or delaying) a traditional Thanksgiving meal at home. However, it will likely be well worth the effort once you see your child giddy with excitement as their favorite cartoon characters float by to the tune of a marching band in full regalia, while giant floats with entertainers glide by at street level.

Note, though, that more than 3.5 million people attend the parade in person each year. It’s important to strategize your visit so you are not far from the curb, struggling to catch a glimpse of the street.

There are several things you’ll want to keep in mind as you plan your day at the parade. Here are our top tips for viewing the 100th annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in 2026.

If you want to get an up-close view of the balloons featured in the annual parade, you won’t want to miss the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Balloon Inflation. The inflation occurs the day before the parade, starting at 1 p.m. on the Upper West Side at 72nd Street and Columbus Avenue, near the American Museum of Natural History. It runs until 6 p.m., so you have several hours to sneak a peek at what’s to come during the parade. (Tip: The line opens at noon.)

There are 32 balloons that will transform from flat to fully inflated during the course of the afternoon. There are some fun new floats to keep an eye out for this year. To name a few, Bob the Minion riding a giant banana, Sorcerer Mickey, the Geico gecko and Earl the Squirrel, a balloon based on a real-life squirrel who made his home in Universal Orlando's Christmas tree several years ago and has now become the park's official holiday mascot.

Inflating a giant balloon the height of a four-story building takes time. Long lines form as the balloons become fully inflated in the early evening, so you may want to test your luck by arriving closer to 3 p.m., when most of the balloons start taking shape.

To get to the event location via public transportation, allow extra time; the subway station at 72nd Street tends to get very crowded as the afternoon wears on. You can also hail a cab or use a ride-hailing service, though you’ll want to be dropped off a block or two north of the gated-off section to avoid delays. Once you're in the line, you'll progress north and can exit west along any block from West 82nd to West 86th streets.

TPG tip: The closest subway station to the entrance point is the B and C stop at 72nd Street and Central Park West. Consider taking the 1, 2 or 3 train to Broadway and 72nd Street instead. It’s a few blocks west but an easy walk — just follow the crowds.

Related: These are the best New York City hotels for families to check out

Some parade-goers arrive as early as 4 a.m. to snag a coveted front-row spot along the route.

Plan accordingly if you have a particular location in mind. For example, prime seats at covered bus stops start filling up around 4 a.m., while you might be able to get front-row curb seating closer to 6 a.m.

Should you have deeper pockets and want to avoid being outside in the elements, you can pay for a parade brunch with a view along the parade route. Just be sure to make these reservations well in advance, as they tend to fill up quickly. Or, of course, you could book a room with a view directly on the parade route.

For those arriving later in the morning, you can stand in the closed-off side streets leading to the parade. You might be 10-15 people back, but you can still see most of the action.

The parade starts at 8:30 a.m. at Central Park West on 77th Street. Since the route is 2.5 miles long, it can take close to an hour for the lead marchers to reach Macy's. This means you’ll have some idle time before you can start watching the spectacle.

Because you could find yourself waiting several hours for the parade to show up, you’ll want to bring some stuff to stay occupied, like snacks, drinks and games. A backup charger is also a good idea.

You can bring camping chairs, buckets or anything else you may want to sit on to the parade, though these items are not very helpful for the parade itself, since most people stand. Still, at the very least, you’ll probably want to have some hotel towels or blankets to sit on instead of the hard, cold, gum-covered New York City sidewalks.

Don’t forget proper attire, including jackets, hats, gloves and umbrellas if rain is in the forecast, since the weather can turn quickly in late fall.

Like at home, excitement builds as the parade start time nears, and before long, cheers erupt as the parade comes into view. However, what you may not realize from watching at home is how interactive the experience can be. You may get high-fives from clowns and even confetti in your hair.

Not everything you see on TV happens along the parade route, either. Some performances, including those by the Radio City Rockettes and various singing and dance groups, only occur in front of Macy’s Herald Square (where the cameras are). As a result, you’ll want to manage your expectations. Don’t worry about what you’re missing. Instead, focus on all that’s taking place in front of you: the floats, balloons and festivities.

Related: 10 tips for flying during the holidays

The parade covers so much of the city that there isn’t one best hotel for attending the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. While some hotels are physically on the parade route, it’s not as simple as booking a room at one of these properties and watching the festivities from your window.

Sure, some windows at the route-adjacent hotels offer good views — but hotels are savvy, so those rooms are often sold as part of pricier parade packages. As such, you’ll have to pay more and often meet minimum stay requirements to see the parade from your actual hotel room.

If you don’t want to splurge to see all the action from your room, ask if your hotel has a special viewing area for guests. Often, hotels on the parade route have some space outside where patrons can watch the parade as it passes.

A few properties on the parade route include:

Should you have trouble securing a room at a property on the parade route or wish to save a little money, consider staying a block or more off the route at properties like The St. Regis New York and Park Hyatt New York. Both are a very short walk to and from the parade.

Some more points-friendly hotels that are within walking distance of the parade route include:

Related: 10 festive hotels for people who really love the holidays

Since New York City is an incredible place to be for the holidays, there are all kinds of other ways to celebrate the season after kicking it off with the parade. Be sure to see Santa in person at Santaland on the eighth floor of Macy’s on 34th Street (reservations are required). The Big Apple Circus, under the big top in Lincoln Center, is a sure-fire family pleaser. Also, peruse some of the festive holiday markets throughout the city when you’re not busy ice skating at Rockefeller Center or catching a performance of a Christmas classic like “The Nutcracker” or “A Christmas Carol.”

#6057. JetBlue Cancels 11 International Routes: See Full List Now

JetBlue is the USA's fourth-largest airline for international service. In November 2026, for example, the carrier has 2,723 departures beyond the US border, equivalent to 91 daily flights. Compared to last November, activity has fallen by 9%.

The international arena is a relatively large part of JetBlue's total offering. In the same month, 20% of services are international, more than double the rate for the US's ten largest operators. However, multiple cuts, including those mentioned in this article, have reduced JetBlue's share from 23% last November.

It is common to compare how things have changed between two periods of time, such as different months, quarters, half years, or years. Cirium Diio data was used to see which international routes JetBlue operated in November 2025 but which do not exist in November 2026.

11 links were identified, most of which existed from New York JFK — historically the airline's most-served airport — and Newark. While they could simply have become seasonal or, at least, focused more on the peak periods, that is not the case. They have all been removed. Moreover, as disclosed recently, JetBlue has pulled out of Antigua, Bonaire, Belize City, and Tulum entirely.

Routes Served Last November But Not This November

Following heavy losses, JetBlue removed many underperforming or less significant international routes network-wise as a part of its JetForward restructuring. Compared to last November, such flights from New York JFK have fallen by a considerable 24%, while Boston (a much smaller station for such activity) is down by 16%. Newark has decreased by 68%, with only one route now served, while Orlando is 29% lower.

Despite the reductions, New York JFK remains JetBlue's number one airport for service beyond the US border. It has 42% of the departures in November, reduced from half 12 months ago. What has really changed is the rise of Fort Lauderdale, at which the carrier is increasingly focusing (internationally and domestically), partly because of the exit of Spirit Airlines.

International flights from the South Florida airport are up 63%, with Fort Lauderdale now accounting for 29% of JetBlue's total, 13 points more than 12 months ago. It is developing a mini-hub, of sorts, between the US and the Caribbean and Latin America. Excluding US territories, 18 international routes are available in November, with more coming in 2027.

One of the two new routes seems to be doing particularly badly, with big changes coming. Find out more here!

Several of the 11 routes were pulled after relatively little time, which is often the case, even without a program like JetForward. If the initial performance is not sufficiently good relative to expectations, and the network contribution is not important enough, it is sensible to redeploy the expensive aircraft to where they may perform better.

New York JFK to San Pedro Sula flights lasted for less than a year, influenced by a very low load factor of just 68.1%. The carrier decided to consolidate on its Fort Lauderdale service, which began in November 2025, with that route's traffic figures rising as a result.

Initial data from the US Department of Transportation demonstrates this. Between November 2025 and the following April, when JFK flights still existed, Fort Lauderdale's average load factor was 62.5%. Ouch. But from May 2026 to August 2026 (as far as the data currently extends), it jumped to 90.1%. Given that more and more lower-yielding transit traffic is probably carried now, yields may have fallen.

#6056. Jeffries puts immigration bill high on Democratic priority list

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., holds a news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call)

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is signaling Democrats will move quickly on immigration legislation when the party reclaims the House in January, while acknowledging it still has work to do in shaping its healthcare agenda.

Jeffries, who is expected to secure his spot as the next speaker during a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday, identified immigration and health care as among the top priorities for the incoming majority during a Tuesday news conference.

“One of the things that we need to do is to move the Dream and Promise Act for DACA recipients and TPS recipients,” Jeffries said, referring to a Democratic bill introduced last year. “We should actually move that bill immediately.”

The proposal aims to create a path to citizenship for certain Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipients and Temporary Protected Status holders. Similar legislation has been a top priority for Democrats in both chambers for more than a decade, with Democrats unable to advance this bill in the House while Republicans have held the majority.

Jeffries also reiterated his calls to rein in Immigration and Customs Enforcement and redirect funding allocated to the agency through Republicans' budget law known as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, while expressing a desire for bipartisan cooperation on immigration more broadly.

“We think the border should be safe and strong and secure, and we think our immigration system overall is broken,” Jeffries said. “We need to fix it in a comprehensive way, and certainly, it's our hope that a handful of Republicans will be willing to join us, so we can fix it in a bipartisan way.”

On healthcare, however, Jeffries offered fewer specifics, suggesting Democrats still have decisions to make before taking control of the chamber. Democrats broadly agree on the need to restore subsidies for plans purchased through health insurance markets that expired at the end of 2025. But the question of what additional steps the party should pursue with the goal of expanding coverage and lowering prices is likely to be a major test of Democratic leadership’s ability to find consensus among its robust new majority.

When asked how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that's all part of an ongoing conversation.”

The New York Democrat outlined several broader healthcare priorities, including reversing Medicaid cuts enacted under President Donald Trump, extending Affordable Care Act tax credits, all of which Democrats have vowed to do over the last year.

“Out of the gate, what we clearly have to do is fix our broken healthcare system in terms of the damage that's been done by Donald Trump and MAGA extremists over the last two years, and that clearly involves reversing the Medicaid cuts and extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits, and beginning to engage in supporting medical research, particularly things like research for pediatric cancer,” Jeffries added.

Democrats established a healthcare working group earlier this Congress, led by Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y. and Terri Sewell, D-Ala., to gather perspectives and develop policy proposals as the party works toward a broader agenda.

Without an announced challenger, Jeffries has expressed confidence that he’ll secure the top Democratic spot in the House, brushing aside questions about incoming members who have said they remain “undecided” ahead of Wednesday’s elections. Jeffries, who was introduced as “Speaker Jeffries” on election night, said last week he was “very confident we’ll get there” and confirmed that the caucus will hold a recorded vote in the contest.

Rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., was nominated for speaker by acclamation ahead of her first election to the position in 2007. But Jeffries’ allies portrayed his decision to go forward with a recorded vote as a show of strength after a group of incoming progressives, many aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America, had floated forcing a recorded vote in the internal leadership race.

Jeffries said Tuesday the approach mirrors the caucus’ 2018 transition from minority to majority, giving members an opportunity to weigh in on who is best positioned to lead based on “track record, experience and vision.”

This report was corrected to reflect Rep. Nancy Pelosi’s status as a current member.

#6055. Malaysia Airlines Orders Up To 16 Boeing 787-10s, Deliveries Start 2032

Malaysia Airlines has just placed a new aircraft order, as the airline will be adding a new wide body aircraft type to its fleet. This seems logical enough, even if the carrier’s long haul fleet seems rather diversified at this point.

Malaysia Airlines has placed its first-ever Dreamliner order, as the airline will be taking delivery of up to 16 Boeing 787-10s. This includes a firm order for 10 jets, plus options for six more, with deliveries expected between 2032 and 2035.

For context, the 787-10 is the largest variant of the Dreamliner. While it has the least range of any 787 variant, the per-seat economics are great, given how it’s “stretched.” While some airlines have started to use the 787-10 for high capacity regional routes, Malaysia Airlines is taking a different approach.

The oneworld carrier intends to use these planes to support its long haul fleet modernization and international expansion, including routes to Europe, along with destinations throughout Asia-Pacific. The airline points out how long haul demand to and from Southeast Asia has increased by more than 50% over the past decade.

Here’s how Malaysia Airlines Group CEO Nasaruddin Bakar describes this:

“The acquisition of the 787 Dreamliner represents a strategic investment in the future of Malaysia Aviation Group. As we look ahead to the next phase of growth, these aircraft will strengthen our ability to serve key international markets with greater capacity, efficiency and flexibility, while delivering the elevated travel experience our customers expect. Beyond fleet renewal, this investment reinforces our commitment to maintaining a modern, competitive airline that supports Malaysia’s connectivity and global aspirations.”

For context, Malaysia Airlines currently has a fleet of just over 90 aircraft, with another 75 aircraft on firm order. As it stands, Malaysia Airlines has:

Now the airline has the following planes on firm order:

A few things stand out here. First of all, it’s cool to see Malaysia Airlines growing again, after a rather rough… what, nearly 15 years? At this point the airline has enough planes on order to both replace its previous generation fleet, and expand. I’d expect the 16 A330ceos will be retired at some point in the coming years, and more than replaced by the A330neos that remain on order. Furthermore, the 737-800s will all be replaced by the 737 MAXs.

The 787-10 is an incredible plane in terms of economics, especially as Boeing has been able to make incremental range improvements, turning it into a true long haul aircraft.

At the same time, I can’t help but feel like it’s unusual how the airline has just seven A350s, with no more on order, and is now switching to the 787 for fleet renewal. Admittedly the A350 was ordered back in the day under a completely different management team, which also at one point thought the A380 was a good fit for the airline.

So I am curious how the carrier’s fleet evolves. Will the seven A350s stick around, or will they eventually just be replaced by 787-10s? Even with airspace restrictions and headwinds, it seems like all of Malaysia Airlines’ routes should be within range for the 787-10, though admittedly London (LHR) might be on the cusp, depending on how airspace closures evolve, how dense of a configuration the airline selects, etc.

The big challenge with the airline industry is that it’s never static, and decisions aren’t made in a vacuum. One management team makes one decision, and then a management team later on can’t just undo what the other management team did, without it being costly. So I get that they’re doing what they can…

Malaysia Airlines is the newest customer for the Boeing 787, as the airline has ordered up to 16 787-10s, including 10 firm orders and six options. The airline plans to use this for a long haul expansion to Europe, as well as for flights in Asia-Pacific.

It’s cool to see Malaysia Airlines continuing to grow, as the carrier has quite the order book at this point. I am curious if the airline keeps around the seven A350s in the long run, or how the airline manages its three wide body aircraft types.

What do you make of Malaysia Airlines’ Boeing 787-10 order?

#6054. SkyWest Pilots Do The Right Thing At SFO, Then Get Snapped At By ATC

With the number of close calls we see at airports nowadays, it’s great to see when pilots or air traffic controllers go above and beyond to be observant, and exhibit good situational awareness. So along those lines, here’s a case of a pilot paying close attention to ensure everyone’s safety, and then an air traffic controller being frustrated by that…

YouTube channel You can see ATC has the air traffic control audio and a visualization of an interaction that happened shortly before noon on November 21, 2026, at San Francisco International Airport (SFO).

In this interaction, a SkyWest Embraer E175 operating on behalf of American Eagle had just landed on runway 28L, after flying from Los Angeles (LAX). The pilots were switched to the ground frequency, and that’s when things quickly went downhill:

The SkyWest pilots then continued their taxi, and when they got to the gate, the conversation continued:

When you screw up, I suppose it’s human nature to get a bit defensive, and I think that’s exactly what happened here.

Credit to the SkyWest pilots for their situational awareness here. They were instructed to taxi in front of another plane, and another plane was instructed to give way to them, but never read back those instructions. The air traffic controller absolutely should have caught that, and as a pilot, they 100% did the correct thing by noticing the lack of a read back, and erring on the side of caution.

This isn’t just some theoretical risk, but ground collisions are the most common kinds of accidents involving commercial aircraft. Could the SkyWest pilots have said “we’re holding short because the other plane didn’t read back instructions?” Sure, but it seems like the time gap here was a matter of seconds, and they didn’t want to step on the radio calls of another pilot, in case they were going to read back.

What I think is really unprofessional is how the air traffic controller then responded to this:

The pilots of a SkyWest flight decided to hold short of a taxiway after they observed the plane that was supposed to give way to them not reading back the correct instructions. That was absolutely the right move, and the air traffic controller should’ve caught that.

When the pilots explained why they held short, the air traffic controller didn’t respond particularly well. Then when they asked for a phone number, she said the pilots would be talking to someone else, and she clearly wasn’t having it. But then she was also mad when the pilot explained very briefly what was going on, saying the conversation should happen off frequency… a conversation she wasn’t willing to have!

This is a clear situation where you have two very professional pilots, and one very unprofessional air traffic controller.

What do you make of this SFO ATC interaction?

#6053. Delta Air Lines Launches 15 New International Routes: See Full List Now

As the northern aviation winter season is here, airlines are increasingly finalizing their plans for next summer. Initial information for Q3 2027 (July-September) shows that Delta Air Lines is planning 258 daily international departures in the all-important period (double for total movements).

The SkyTeam member's offering is currently expected to be 6% higher than for Q3 2026, with 14 daily departures added. It will be the seventh-highest volume on record for that quarter. However, it is subject to change, as Delta firms up its plan. Still, 15 new and returning routes will help, some of which will be operating in the third quarter of 2027, having not done so in 2026.

For this article, Delta's international network in Q3 2026 was compared to what is planned for Q3 2027 using Cirium Diio data. 15 international routes were identified, eight of which are long-haul. As all markets have already been officially announced, this article simply summarizes what is happening and provides some additional context.

Only routes that have already been disclosed and are scheduled are included. As such, any upcoming new link from Seattle, expected to be revealed on December 2, is excluded. While flights to Singapore have been increasingly speculated, this is not entirely certain. Even so, it is unclear when, precisely, they'd begin.

Medium & Long-Haul Routes: Didn't Operate In Q3 2026 But Will In Q3 2027

A brand-new market. The launch was postponed for half a year. Suggestions that this will be delayed to the second half of 2027

A brand-new market. It'll connect the Texas capital with the hugely important European SkyTeam hub. It'll be Delta's only long-haul route from Austin. Interestingly, flights will arrive in Texas at 4:52 PM and leave at 3:15 PM. Is another route coming?!

Previously served in 2021. Replaces Detroit-Reykjavík Keflavík, which Delta last served in 2026. Delta ended that route shortly after Icelandair did. Boston-Reykjavík Keflavík will be the airline's new shortest route to Europe

A brand-new market. Venice is the largest unserved European city from Boston

A brand-new market. The capital of Greece is the #1 unserved European market from Detroit

New for Delta, but Northwest flew via Tokyo Narita until 2009 using the 747-400. Delta flew to the Philippines via Narita until 2020, just not beginning/ending in Los Angeles

Inherited from Northwest. Delta previously operated until 2020

None of the following links are brand-new, which is perhaps not surprising. None of them are new to Delta's map in 2026, although two links were inaugurated in December 2025. They include Austin to Los Cabos, with Delta joining American (albeit only January, March, and April 2027) and Southwest. In Q3 2027, Delta's offering contributes to that market having a record number of flights.

Many of the entries are markets that Delta already serves. They are simply included because flights did not operate in Q3 2026 but are scheduled to do so in the same quarter next year. In many ways, this is a vote of confidence for a route. Obviously, the reverse (a shorter operating period with fewer flights and less capacity) may indicate problems. Just ask Southwest about one of its links to Alaska.

Short-Haul Routes: Didn't Operate In Q3 2026 But Will In Q3 2027

Route operated between December 2025 and April 2026. It didn't run in Q3 last year, but will now do so

Weekly to daily A321ceo, 737-800, 737-900ER

For obvious reasons, Delta's total flights on the aging, fuel-inefficient, maintenance-heavy, but clearly characterful Boeing 757 have fallen dramatically in recent years. Only 8,455 movements are scheduled on the 757-200 and 757-300 in Q3 2027, down by 60% compared to Q3 2026. Retirements have contributed to this reduction, while nine A321neos were delivered in September and October 2026 alone.

The decrease is due to the domestic market (-67% year-over-year). In contrast, 30% more international 757 flights are planned between next July and September, although this is still far below historic levels. This is not because of the relaunch of service from Boston to Iceland after a five-year absence, as that is just replacing the 757 link from Detroit to the nation. In contrast, Q3 flights from Los Angeles to Mexico City do contribute, although this is only one part of the picture.

#6052. Senators still see NDAA as chance for online safety legislation

Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., delivers his opening statement during the hearing on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call)

Online safety advocates are looking to the annual defense policy bill for action on legislation to expand accountability for online platforms in cases of child sexual exploitation, as they also introduced legislation to make sure those cases aren’t forced into private arbitration.

Senators and advocates expressed support Tuesday for legislation that would expand the ability of victims of online sexual exploitation to sue social media platforms at a hearing focused on dangers children face on the gaming platform Roblox.

The Senate Judiciary Committee’s panel on Crime and Counterterrorism held the hearing after its Chairman Josh Hawley, R-Mo., and ranking member Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., introduced a bill Monday that would ban pre-dispute arbitration agreements from affecting cases where a minor was harmed online, including by sexual exploitation.

Hawley and Durbin also worked together on a separate bill to expand eligibility for victims of abuse to bring civil suits against online platforms that intentionally, knowingly or recklessly promoted or facilitated the abuse. It would also include penalties for certain platforms that fail to report child pornography violations on their sites.

That bill is included in a manager’s amendment to the Senate’s fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act bill. Durbin encouraged Congress to pass the NDAA “in the closing days” of the session because “protecting children is an important part of it.”

“I have a few weeks left in my service in the United States Senate,” said Durbin, who is retiring at the end of his term in January. “I’m thinking each day it’s coming to an end, but I want it to come [to an] end the right way.”

The subcommittee has spent much of the 119th Congress focused on harms to children online, including from artificial intelligence chatbots.

Tuesday’s hearing included testimony from survivors and experts on child exploitation on Roblox.

Hawley said that victims are bound by pre-dispute agreements with Roblox to settle claims through private arbitration, rather than in court.

“They slam the courthouse door shut in their faces,” Hawley said. “We’re talking about children now, child victims of sexual exploitation online are denied their day in court by the very company that has exposed them to the content to begin with.”

A spokesperson for Roblox said in a statement that “safety has been central” to the platform since its launch.

“We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age-based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat,” the spokesperson said. “A legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a company’s safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety.”

Myriam Gilles, a professor of law at Northwestern University, told the panel that a 2022 law that ended forced arbitration agreements for victims of sexual assault has gaps. She said Roblox has argued it does not apply to online actions, just “completed physical assault” and does not apply to platforms.

She also said that Hawley’s new arbitration bill would enhance the effects of his measure regarding civil suits by making sure those suits can be heard publicly if families so choose.

“Congress can pass laws, but if [suits] just get shunted into private arbitration, they’re doing no good in the world,” Gilles said. “A right to sue that ends in secret arbitration is a right in name only.”

The hearing came the same day that advocates, including reality TV personality and activist Paris Hilton, held a press conference to urge House action on a bill (S 1837) that would allow individuals to bring civil suits over nonconsensual intimate depictions generated by artificial intelligence or for possession or production of deepfake porn if there was also intent to disclose the images.

That bill passed the Senate in January but has not been taken up in the House.

#6051. Why JetBlue Is My Favorite Way To Fly Economy Across The Atlantic

I’ve flown back and forth across the Atlantic dozens of times in all cabins, including many times in economy. JetBlue definitely stands out as being my favorite, and dare I say it, the most premium of all the transatlantic economy flights I’ve experienced.

My most recent trip was from Europe to Boston (BOS) for the opening of JetBlue’s newest BlueHouse location. The airline covered my flights for the event, but had no input in this article. I’d like to share some of the reasons that JetBlue’s transatlantic experience impressed me so much.

Economy class meals can seem like quite the downgrade should one be accustomed to the elevated fare at the pointy end of the plane.

JetBlue currently partners with NYC-based Dig Inn for its transatlantic economy-class meals, and they’re far better than average. They also offer products from a range of interesting brands, rather than just your classic soda labels.

Here’s an example of the drinks menu on my flight from Amsterdam to Boston.

Meals are served in these stylish, reusable, matte-black sealed containers. I’d love to see more airlines do more to reduce their waste like this.

I was very happy with my choice of chicken pesto pasta salad as the main course, accompanied by sides of beet and carrot slaw and snap peas with feta. The fresh, flavorful, yet cold dishes were far better than many of the reheated slop I’ve been served in economy before.

I was equally impressed by the breakfast I had on the morning departure back from Boston to London Heathrow (LHR). I went for the Bubly sparkling water again, as I avoid coffee on a plane unless it’s served as espresso. The stuff they pour out of those vats is pretty much just glorified dirty water.

As far as pre-landing light meals go, this pizza thing was pretty good, too.

In addition to the main meal and pre-landing light bite, JetBlue keeps a well-stocked pantry at the back of the Airbus A321LR.

JetBlue has been offering fast, free, in-flight Wi-Fi for as long as I can remember. The same cannot be said for some full-service carriers, which still can’t guarantee a reliable, fast, and free connection on their transatlantic flights.

They’ve also added some fun tech features, like the ability to choose the elements for the main meal service via the IFE screen, even in economy. I think it has a more premium feel than being asked “chicken or beef?”

I’m not a frequent JetBlue flyer, so I couldn’t really make the most of the fun personalization features, such as the option to continue watching the movie where you left off on your last flight.

Being given anything more than the standard pillow and blanket in economy is a rare bonus. It had been so long since my last JetBlue flight in economy that I’d forgotten about the complimentary Snooze Kit.

I prefer to use my AirPods to earplugs, but I did make good use of the eye mask for a mid-flight nap.

I’ve flown over my fair share of narrow bodies on long-haul flights, and I genuinely don’t know why such a fuss is made about them being terrible.

JetBlue’s version of the aircraft has comfy seats, with standard Core (economy) seats having 32 inches of pitch. Another common complaint I hear is that there are fewer toilets. For a plane with far fewer passengers (only 114 in economy), fewer toilets kind of makes sense. I didn’t once find myself waiting in line to use the bathroom on either flight.

For what it’s worth, there are two lavatories for 114 economy passengers, so that’s one lavatory per 57 passengers. That’s a little lower than the industry standard, but not by much. For example, American’s standard 787-9s have five lavatories for 255 economy seats, so that’s a ratio of one lavatory per 51 passengers.

If you’ve only got the budget or the points for economy for your next trip to Europe, I couldn’t recommend JetBlue more. They now fly to eight cities in Europe, the planes are comfortable and modern, and the in-flight food and beverage is top of the game for economy.

What do you make of JetBlue’s transatlantic economy offering?

#6050. Hill GOP looking to trim White House's $50 billion aviation ask

Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy conducts a news conference on the recent nationwide ground stop after meeting with Senate Republicans in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

Senate Republicans poured cold water Tuesday on the administration’s new ask for a $50.1 billion emergency air traffic control and airport infrastructure package, arguing much of it has little to do with the immediate problems that led to a nationwide ground stop on Friday.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought last week asked for $30.1 billion before Duffy voiced support for the rest of the funds at a Friday night press conference on the ground stop.

The original ask contained roughly $12 billion that was tied directly to air traffic control upgrades, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said, with the remainder going toward long-sought airport terminal and other upgrades to aging aviation facilities.

Duffy and Vought laid out in a letter to House and Senate appropriators on Tuesday what the extra $20 billion would be for — half for construction of five new air route traffic control centers, and half for construction, replacement and improvement of up to 140 air traffic control towers.

They justified the increased demand because of the “urgent need” that became evident after the ground stop. Duffy and Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford fanned out across the Capitol to try to sell the request, including a stop at Senate Republicans’ weekly policy lunch.

But it quickly became evident that their own allies on Capitol Hill want more and better justification for why so much extra money is needed.

Not only are there concerns that much of the request would go to terminal reconstruction and other longer-term projects, but lawmakers keep noting the FAA hasn’t yet spent about $8 billion out of the initial $12.5 billion “down payment” on air traffic control modernization provided in last year’s budget reconciliation law.

“I don’t think the full $50 billion will be funded,” Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, said Tuesday. “What we just discussed there, and what I expressed, is that the request needs to be focused on safety modernization.”

Still, Cruz said the administration had done a “good job” with the initial $12.5 billion modernization plan so far and he expected to see continued bipartisan support for the effort.

Senate Republicans are considering adding additional aviation funds through a filibuster-proof reconciliation bill, a process that could begin as soon as this week with a floor “vote-a-rama” on a resolution to unlock that process. Cruz said that while reconciliation could be the vehicle used, additional aviation funds need to be “safety-focused.”

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said after the lunch with Duffy and Bedford that he expects Congress will look at a package more in the $10 billion to $30 billion range.

For his part, Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., said the airline industry itself should foot at least a portion of the bill, considering how much federal support the carriers have received over the years.

“I don't understand why the airline industry doesn't pay for it. We give them unbelievable amounts of money,” Scott said, adding that he doesn’t like adding to the deficit and is “not big on government running things.”

Duffy explained the need for the high price tag as the result of decades of pent-up demand that are now threatening major disruptions and safety risks to the traveling public.

“This has never been done. To be clear, we are keeping planes safe in the sky, and we are switching out equipment that’s been a problem for decades,” he said. “I and the president have decided we are going to lean in and fix it.”

He called the effort a “historic investment” reflecting the ways air travel has changed since much of the nation’s infrastructure was built — noting that the newest tower was constructed in 1969 and much of the software being used is from the 1990s. Still, Duffy said, on the current course of funding, it would take 300 years to replace every U.S. tower.

“I'm not going to tell [Congress] how to do their work, but I'm telling everybody what we need,” Duffy said. “And whether it's a party-line vote or if it's a bipartisan vote, I do think this is one moment in a very charged political environment — one moment where almost all Americans and bipartisan members of both bodies are kind of in agreement that we should lean in to do this.”

Even as Duffy petitioned for additional funds Tuesday, he said that the “root cause” of the equipment instability that made the ground stop necessary is still unclear as investigators analyze the router that caused the problem.

A “routine switchover” from old copper wires to digital fiber in the telecommunications system “started to create issues in our network,” Duffy explained Tuesday.

The telecommunications transition includes the conversion of thousands of routers to what are known as Juniper devices — a process being undertaken by contractor L3Harris Technologies. Duffy and Bedford explained that 68 other routers had been converted without incident prior to the problematic switchover Friday.

Bedford said Tuesday that use of the router that officials have identified as the source of the system instability has been suspended “and we've disabled the ones that are out there.”

The decision to suspend use of the router followed an inquiry sent to the agency by Senate Commerce Committee Democrats a day prior. “With thousands of conversions remaining, FAA must address outstanding safety and reliability concerns before expanding installation,” they wrote.

Bedford said he was “highly confident” that similar problems wouldn’t erupt again. “Every element of this is going to be analyzed to see what we learn here and make sure that it doesn't get repeated,” he said.

David Jordan, Lia Chien and Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

#6049. British Airways Visa Card Review: Is It Worth The $95 Annual Fee?

The British Airways Visa Signature® Card is one of Chase’s co-branded airline credit cards, and British Airways Club is certainly a popular frequent flyer program, given the overall value of the Avios ecosystem, plus the number of destinations in the United States that British Airways serves.

Who should be applying for the British Airways Visa, and under what circumstances is it worth spending money on it? Let’s take a look at what you need to know about this card, and what the best alternatives are.

Link: Learn more about the British Airways Visa Signature® Card

Before jumping into a closer look at every aspect of the British Airways Visa Card, here’s a high-level view of the card’s key features, perks, and fees:

Here are my thoughts on the biggest British Airways Visa Card pros and cons:

If you’re considering the British Airways Visa Signature Card, its welcome bonus, application rules, and annual fee are all probably top of mind. So let’s start by taking a look at these important details.

The British Airways Visa currently offers the following welcome bonus: Earn 75,000 Avios after you spend $5,000 on purchases within the first three months of account opening.

Based on my current points and miles valuations, which put Avios at 1.2 cents apiece, this current bonus is worth about $900. That’s a pretty solid welcome bonus, especially for a card with a moderate annual fee.

The British Airways Visa has a $95 annual fee. This is not waived for the first year, and there’s no additional fee to add authorized users.

British Airways’ credit card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s potentially a great card to use for purchases abroad.

The welcome bonus on the British Airways Visa isn’t available to those who currently have the card, or those who have received a new cardmember bonus on the card in the past 24 months. You are eligible for this card if you’ve had the Iberia Visa Signature® Card and/or Aer Lingus Visa Signature® Card, despite the similarities between the cards.

Chase’s other general policies on card approvals apply as well, including the 5/24, whereby you generally won’t be approved for a Chase card if you’ve opened five or more credit cards in the last 24 months.

The British Airways Visa Card has no foreign transaction fees, but does the rewards structure warrant putting spending on the card? It might, but only thanks to additional bonuses offered by the card, which incentivize spending.

The British Airways Visa doesn’t have terribly exciting bonus categories. You earn:

There are lots of great credit cards for airfare purchases and hotel purchases. This isn’t a card I would be putting much spending on unless you’re trying to earn a Travel Together Ticket, in which case it could definitely be worth it. More on that below.

British Airways Club is a transfer partner of Amex Membership Rewards, Bilt Rewards, Capital One, and Chase Ultimate Rewards, so it could make sense to put spending on a card earning one of those currencies if you want to earn Avios at an accelerated rate.

There are lots of great uses of British Airways Avios. British Airways Club has roughly distance based award pricing, and the program offers value in situations where other programs might not. Generally speaking, here’s where I see value with Avios:

British Airways is known for adding large taxes and surcharges to some of its own award flights, so this is worth keeping in mind.

Personally I find Avios to be one of the most useful frequent flyer programs for redeeming points, thanks to the number of redemptions this opens up.

Often one of the big challenges people have with points is figuring out how to pool them since you typically need enough points in a single account for a redemption. A cool feature of the British Airways Club program is that you can form household accounts. This allows you to pool the Avios you earn with up to six other people registered at the same address as you.

This is especially awesome in the context of a credit card welcome bonus, since you can pool a ton of Avios in a single account if you have two people get for the card in a household, etc.

There are some benefits to the British Airways Visa Card that could alone justify having this card. For some people, it will be worth spending money on the card to unlock some perks, while for others just having the card and not spending money on it offers sufficient benefits. Let’s look at what those benefits are, and how they work.

One of the best benefits of the British Airways Signature Visa is that it offers a 10% discount on British Airways flights starting in the United States. To take advantage of this, just book through ba.com/chase10, and use your card to pay while using promotion code BACHASE10.

If you fly British Airways with any frequency, this could cover the annual fee over and over. See this post for everything you need to know about the British Airways Visa flight discount.

If you have the British Airways Visa Card and redeem Avios for a reward flight, you can receive up to $600 in statement credits annually. You can earn up to three statement credits, as follows:

There are some basic terms to be aware of:

British Airways now also offers Reward Flight Saver from the United States, allowing you to redeem more Avios and pay lower surcharges. Getting a further statement credit of up to $200 on that is pretty great.

One of the potentially great perks of the British Airways Visa is that you can earn a Travel Together Ticket when you spend $30,000 on the card in a calendar year.

This companion ticket will be deposited in your British Airways Club account four to six weeks after you’ve completed the required spending.

With this certificate, you can book a British Airways award ticket at the full cost of Avios (plus taxes, fees, and surcharges), and then for the second passenger you don’t have to pay any Avios, but rather just have to pay all the fees.

This also offers a lot of flexibility — you can also use the voucher as a solo traveler and get 50% off the Avios required for a ticket. Your ticket can originate anywhere in the world, and you can even travel on Aer Lingus or Iberia.

This can represent a fantastic deal for first and business class travel, given how much those tickets would otherwise cost. This isn’t for everyone, though it has the potential to represent a good value, and I know it’s a feature that many value.

See this post for everything you need to know about the British Airways Visa companion voucher.

As a Visa Signature card, the British Airways Visa comes with the following shopping and travel protection benefits:

You’ll want to review the card’s benefits guide for any exclusions and rules that apply.

The British Airways Visa Card has a solid welcome bonus, and that could be a legitimate motivator for picking up this card. However, personally this isn’t a card I would use for everyday spending, since you can earn British Airways Avios at a better rate with other American Express or Chase cards. It also lacks a few benefits that many other airline credit cards offer, including a free checked bag and priority boarding.

That said, I absolutely think this card is worth holding onto if you fly British Airways with any frequency because:

There are several Avios currencies, with three belonging to International Airlines Group (IAG) airlines — there’s British Airways, Aer Lingus, and Iberia. There are also two other US-based credit cards that directly earn Avios from these airlines. Specifically, we’re talking about the Iberia Visa Card (learn more) and Aer Lingus Visa Card (learn more).

Which of these cards should you select? They have a lot in common:

The differences mainly come in the form of the perks associated with just holding onto the cards, and also the perks associated with spending $30,000 on the cards in a calendar year:

The best card to select comes down to which benefits you value most. Also, remember that you’re eligible for all three of these cards, should you be interested, so you don’t necessarily have to choose between them.

See here for a full comparison of cards earning Avios.

If you want to earn British Airways Avios, I’d recommend getting a card that earns either Amex Membership Rewards, Bilt Rewards, Capital One, or Chase Ultimate Rewards points. Here’s why:

With that in mind, which cards should you consider? Here are some of my favorite Chase Ultimate Rewards-earning cards:

If you’re over 5/24 or simply prefer Amex points or Capital One miles, here are some top choices:

The British Airways Visa is one of the best co-branded airline credit cards out there, in my opinion. The card offers a solid welcome bonus, and it can be worth spending money on the card to earn a companion ticket.

Beyond that, the card can be worth having for the discounts offered on both paid tickets (up to 10% off) or award tickets (up to $200 in statement credits), which can cover the annual fee over and over. That said, the card would be even stronger if it offered a free checked bag and lounge access as benefits — though I’d expect the annual to increase if those were added, especially the latter perk.

When it comes to earning British Airways Avios long term, personally I’d much rather earn Amex, Bilt, Capital One, and Chase points, and transfer them to British Airways. Not only does this allow you to earn points at a much faster rate, but it also gives you a lot more flexibility.

If you’re looking for more travel deals, check out our roundup of the best hotel deals currently available.

Air Canada's Worldwide Seat Sale discounts flights from the U.S. to Canada, Mexico, the Caribbean, Central and South America and Asia-Pacific (excluding India), in cash or Aeroplan points. Book by Nov. 29 for travel between Nov. 30, 2026, and Sept. 30, 2027.

New Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® cardholders can earn 50% bonus points on purchases in categories that normally earn 1x (up to 20,000 bonus points), and Aeroplan members get 10,000 points off hotel redemptions and 15,000 off car rentals when redeeming 50,000 points or more (codes "BFHOTEL26" and "BFAUTO26," through Nov. 30).

You can also expect some special offers for American Airlines AAdvantage members, so be sure to check back on Friday.

Alaska Airlines has announced it will offer some good Black Friday deals, but you'll need to wait until Friday to see the details.

You can also expect some great points deals using Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards points.

Allegiant is offering a big Black Friday sale. We don't yet have details, but last year, fares dropped as low as $39 one-way.

Avelo Airlines is offering a special early Black Friday deal for members of "Plus" — the carrier's paid loyalty membership program that costs $59 for the first year (and $99 per year after).

You can get 90% off base fares on select flights for travel through April 20, 2027.

No code is needed, but as stated, you'll need to be a Plus member.

The sale ends the night of Nov. 25, 2026.

BermudAir and its affiliate AnguillAir are offering 30% off flights to Bermuda and Anguilla for Black Friday, Cyber Monday and Travel Tuesday when you use promo code "BLACK30" for travel dates between Dec. 1 and April 30, 2027. (Blackout dates apply.)

You can also get 75% off the base fare when you bundle flights and hotels with BermudAir Holidays when visiting Bermuda, Anguilla, Belize, Providenciales, South Caicos and Guatemala.

Breeze Airways has a Black Friday sale that gets travelers as much as $100 off round-trip flights when using the promo code "WISHLIST" from Friday, Nov. 27 through Sunday, Nov. 29. That's up to 60% off its base fares.

British Airways has flight and vacation deals for travel from the U.S. to London and several other top European destinations. Round-trip coach fares start at $623 and span across many dates. Customers can also save on vacation packages.

Delta will be offering a big Cyber Monday sale on Monday, Nov. 30, lasting through Dec. 2. Stay tuned for more details. Meanwhile, Delta already has some holiday offers available now.

Delta SkyMiles members can boost their rewards balances by earning bonus miles — at a rate of up to 5 miles per dollar spent — on Delta gift card purchases of $400 or more.

The United Arab Emirates' national carrier is offering discounts of up to 20% across many of its routes, bookable through Dec. 1.

Fiji Airways is offering Black Friday deals, with flights as low as $899 round-trip on nonstop flights from Dallas, Los Angeles and San Francisco to Nadi, Fiji, and then on to Sydney and Auckland.

JetBlue is offering one of its biggest sales of the year this Black Friday, including flights for as few as 3,200 JetBlue TrueBlue points.

BlueFirst — JetBlue's first-class awards — start at fewer than 20,000 points each way. You can also score as much as $800 off vacation packages.

Singapore Airlines will host a fun Black Friday sale, with details to be released soon. The airline usually offers discounts of between 15% and 20% on all cabins from U.S. cities to Asia.

TAP Air Portugal is offering some great deals on fares to Europe from various U.S. airports. Prices start at $226 each way in economy, and there are some deals in business class. The sale ends Dec. 2.

Southwest has a Cyber Week sale, with details to be released after Black Friday. #6046. Woman Faced A Felony Charge For Stealing A Rental Car—Then Won A Seat In Congress And Prosecutors Dropped The Case

This year was such a wave election that in some cases candidate quality didn’t matter at all. It was enough to win just not to be a Republican. Shortly before the election, Democratic congressional candidate LaKesha Womack pulled into a high school parking lot in North Carolina for a Sunday rally. A sheriff’s deputy pulled up behind her. He handed her a felony summons for stealing a Toyota Corolla she’d rented from Budget nearly seven years earlier. The incumbent congressman she was running against turned the rental into a television ad. She won anyway. And on Tuesday, after Budget got paid for the six weeks its car was overdue, the district attorney dropped the charge for good. It’s good to get elected to Congress. Budget Car Rental Got The Corolla Back In 2019 Womack picked up the car in Charlotte on August 27, 2019, and renewed the rental twice. Her last extension began October 7, 2019. According to the police report the vehicle was due back at noon on October 23. On November 26 an officer reported that police couldn’t find her and put out an all points bulletin. Police recovered the Corolla and returned it to Budget on December 4, 42 days late. Budget sold the vehicle the following year. Womack has a number of excuses for never returning the car. She says a diabetic seizure and long hospitalization had wiped her out financially. (It’s not clear why that kept her from returning it.) Her son went into foster care while she was in the hospital (again, unclear why that kept her from returning it) and the two of them wound up living in a hotel (hotels have parking, but the hotel didn’t force her to keep the car). She’d expected the company to come get the car. She says she had nowhere reliable to receive mail (when you rent a car you know you’re supposed to give it back, even without a mailed notice) and she thought the matter was settled (exactly how it would have been is unclear). On January 14, 2020, a court issued a summons for felony failure to return the car. Under North Carolina law, willfully keeping a rental vehicle past its deadline is a felony if the vehicle is worth more than $4,000. The car was valued at $20,000. Womack says she first heard about the case on Friday, October 9, 2026. A local reporter posted the records. She responded, “I do owe them people some money, obviously.” BREAKING: Documents pulled from the NC Courts government website show District 14 congressional candidate Lakesha Womack has a “pending” felony warrant for failure to return a rental car in 2019. Police records say Budget Car Rental rented a car to Womack on Oct. 7, 2019 and it was supposed be returned on Oct 23, 2019. Pics and links attached. https://t.co/4WZRvweFxM — Brett Jensen WBT News (@Brett_Jensen) October 9, 2026 Two days later, on October 11, the summons was reissued. A Polk County deputy’s body camera caught the handoff outside the county Democratic rally. Republican Congressman Tim Moore ran an ad on this. Watch Tim Moore’s campaign ad, “Keep Your Money.” He Helped Draw The District. She Didn’t Even Live In It. Moore spent ten years as speaker of the North Carolina House, helped gerrymander the district to favor Republicans and won it in 2024 by nearly 65,000 votes. Womack, an ordained minister making her first run for public office, lived in a neighboring district and said she had no plans to move. A House member only has to live in the state. Through October 14, Moore had spent $1,921,880 to Womack’s $55,626. He spent nearly $1 million on ads. She had no paid full-time staff and didn’t buy a TV spot. Three days after the deputy served her she was handing out T-shirts to striking workers at Charlotte Douglas airport. Moore won five of the six counties. He even won the Election Day vote by 21,246. But early in-person voting, which started four days after the deputy showed up, gave Womack a 24,700 vote lead. With the felony case still pending, she posted, “#HatersGonnaHate I’m still Congresswoman-Elect.” On November 16 prosecutors learned she’d reached a deal with Budget. She paid the assessed rental cost for the overdue period. Budget told prosecutors it was satisfied. Campaign donations may not have mattered in the race, but that’s an unusually inexpensive way to buy goodwill with a member of the U.S. House of Representatives. On November 24 the state dismissed the charge with prejudice. This Wasn’t Hertz When I first wrote about Womack on October 11, my entire comment was “Ruh roh – it wasn’t Hertz.” A reader guessed Budget had lost track of a car it already had back. A father and his 13-year-old daughter were held at gunpoint outside Savannah in a car they’d just rented from Hertz’s Thrifty brand. When police let the father show them his rental agreement, it was 36 minutes old. The car had been reported stolen before Thrifty handed him the keys. A Hertz President’s Circle member wound up in jail over a Salt Lake City rental he’d extended, returned and paid $3,900 for. Those arrest stories seemed to dry up after Hertz brought in Palantir to help track its fleet in 2022 and agreed to pay $168 million to settle 364 claims. At Least Womack Was Still Campaigning North Carolina Republicans drew a map they expected would give them 11 of the state’s 14 U.S. House seats. Democrats won 11. Elsewhere the wave carried a couple of candidates who’d actually stopped campaigning. In Iowa, Eric Armstrong suspended his state House campaign on September 7 for health reasons. He beat a county supervisor and retired police lieutenant by about ten points. In Texas, Ericka Lomick suspended her campaign when a federal mortgage fraud conviction raised questions about whether she could serve. Her name stayed on the ballot for both the rest of the outgoing state representative’s term and the next one. She beat the same Republican in both elections. He’s asked the Texas Supreme Court to block certification of the special election. In California, Womack’s $55,626 would’ve looked like a fortune to Hipolito Cerros. The 28-year-old former mayor raised no campaign money, hired no staff and bought no ads. He unseated the Republican leader of the state Assembly. Tennessee tech support worker Victoria Broderick lost to Congressman Scott DesJarlais in 2024. He took 70% of the vote. After Republicans redrew the district, she ran again. She was still working full time and had to message her boss the morning after the election. The race was called for her the same day Womack’s charge was dropped. My personal favorite this cycle is Maricopa County, Arizona’s Sebastian Matta – a 19-year-old Arizona State philosophy sophomore – who beat a former state senator to become clerk of the Superior Court. He’d filed his campaign finance paperwork late and blamed his accountant for going quiet on him. He’ll run an office that processes 15,000 documents a day. To rent a Corolla from Budget at the Phoenix airport, he’s still two years short of the usual minimum age. In 2012, the anti-gay Democrat running as the incumbent for state representative in Hutchinson, Kanasa defeated her primary challenger – an openly gay son of a former member of the Ku Klux Klan – and then went on to best her Republican opponent who was a pro-gay rights, pro-choice train conductor named Dakota Bass. That race was featured in season two, episode eight of The Newsroom. (HT: Paul H.) Through October 14, Moore had spent $1,921,880 to Womack’s $55,626. He spent nearly $1 million on ads. She had no paid full-time staff and didn’t buy a TV spot. Three days after the deputy served her she was handing out T-shirts to striking workers at Charlotte Douglas airport. Moore won five of the six counties. He even won the Election Day vote by 21,246. But early in-person voting, which started four days after the deputy showed up, gave Womack a 24,700 vote lead. With the felony case still pending, she posted, “#HatersGonnaHate I’m still Congresswoman-Elect.” On November 16 prosecutors learned she’d reached a deal with Budget. She paid the assessed rental cost for the overdue period. Budget told prosecutors it was satisfied. Campaign donations may not have mattered in the race, but that’s an unusually inexpensive way to buy goodwill with a member of the U.S. House of Representatives. On November 24 the state dismissed the charge with prejudice. This Wasn’t Hertz When I first wrote about Womack on October 11, my entire comment was “Ruh roh – it wasn’t Hertz.” A reader guessed Budget had lost track of a car it already had back. A father and his 13-year-old daughter were held at gunpoint outside Savannah in a car they’d just rented from Hertz’s Thrifty brand. When police let the father show them his rental agreement, it was 36 minutes old. The car had been reported stolen before Thrifty handed him the keys. A Hertz President’s Circle member wound up in jail over a Salt Lake City rental he’d extended, returned and paid $3,900 for. Those arrest stories seemed to dry up after Hertz brought in Palantir to help track its fleet in 2022 and agreed to pay $168 million to settle 364 claims. At Least Womack Was Still Campaigning North Carolina Republicans drew a map they expected would give them 11 of the state’s 14 U.S. House seats. Democrats won 11. Elsewhere the wave carried a couple of candidates who’d actually stopped campaigning. In Iowa, Eric Armstrong suspended his state House campaign on September 7 for health reasons. He beat a county supervisor and retired police lieutenant by about ten points. In Texas, Ericka Lomick suspended her campaign when a federal mortgage fraud conviction raised questions about whether she could serve. Her name stayed on the ballot for both the rest of the outgoing state representative’s term and the next one. She beat the same Republican in both elections. He’s asked the Texas Supreme Court to block certification of the special election. In California, Womack’s $55,626 would’ve looked like a fortune to Hipolito Cerros. The 28-year-old former mayor raised no campaign money, hired no staff and bought no ads. He unseated the Republican leader of the state Assembly. Tennessee tech support worker Victoria Broderick lost to Congressman Scott DesJarlais in 2024. He took 70% of the vote. After Republicans redrew the district, she ran again. She was still working full time and had to message her boss the morning after the election. The race was called for her the same day Womack’s charge was dropped. My personal favorite this cycle is Maricopa County, Arizona’s Sebastian Matta – a 19-year-old Arizona State philosophy sophomore – who beat a former state senator to become clerk of the Superior Court. He’d filed his campaign finance paperwork late and blamed his accountant for going quiet on him. He’ll run an office that processes 15,000 documents a day. To rent a Corolla from Budget at the Phoenix airport, he’s still two years short of the usual minimum age. In 2012, the anti-gay Democrat running as the incumbent for state representative in Hutchinson, Kanasa defeated her primary challenger – an openly gay son of a former member of the Ku Klux Klan – and then went on to best her Republican opponent who was a pro-gay rights, pro-choice train conductor named Dakota Bass. That race was featured in season two, episode eight of The Newsroom. (HT: Paul H.) The poor people of NC, having this criminal “representing” them.

Summarizing: – Woman didn’t return rental car as per her contract. (Theft? Conversion? Breach of contract? The first two are criminal.) – Prosecutor drops carges [coincidentally?] once she’s elected – Woman shows no remorse

I’m confident if I got the summary wrong someone will correct me.

#1: I’m going for Theft as a minimum, police report justified, and prosecutor charges as well. Later had her attitude been better than “well maybe I should have returned THEIR car” (paraphrased) maybe walk it down to breach of contract or misunderstanding.

#2: Her getting elected changes no facts on the ground. She rented a car. She signed a rental contract. She failed to abide by it, and “kept the car” beyond her right to keep that car. The prosecutor rightly carged her, but the story doesnt seem to indicate WHICH charges were filed? And yet once elected the prosecutor dropped the charges. Why? (that’s a whole lot of question involving a who, a why, and a why now and not before or after.)

Is this justice? I I rent a car and don’t return it and the cops stop me I should be overjoyed to stay alive. Apparently she’s in a “better class of people” who can jocularly opine that maybe she should have returned the car.

I don’t know whom she represents, but I didn’t vote for her, and wouldn’t.

WAIT! So she’s actually a case where the person DID steal the car, and THIS is the time the rental car company decides to drop it.

I’m here for the comments defending her keeping the car.

Hmmmm . . . sitting on this for 7 years AFTER they recovered the car. I’m sure this is entirely coincidental and had nothing to do with the election. This is one of the clearest cases of a simple civil matter at this point for monetary damages. No chance in hell there wasn’t some political instigation to any criminal charges suddenly becoming alive again nearly 7 years after they got the car back.

@David – the felony summons was issued six years ago. The felony wasn’t invented because she was running for Congress. She stole a car!

When she got caught she write the car rental company a check and claims she had diabetes so it’s ok for her to steal a car. Democrats are indeed above the law!

Keeping the car, or simply failing to return the car for a while?

This looks like the latter. A whole bunch of problems, returning the car wasn’t high on her priorities. It was returned, I do not see criminal **intent**, I see someone overwhelmed. I doubt I would vote guilty, but I doubt I would vote for her in the election. This was not exactly good judgment.

L3 The poor people of the United States having a criminal leading them.

Bold decision-makers that aren’t afraid of taking risks tend to make great leaders.

She is likely a one term event and will draw a primary opponent next cycle It was a yellow dog election — people voted for anything that was not an R.

Shit happens. When shit happens to poor people, it happens a lot worse.

Now, do I know that her excuses are legit or not? I do not. But in our country, if you are living paycheck to paycheck like most American workers, and you get sick, and you are hospitalized, you lose everything, and you have to prioritize, and maybe not returning a rental car is your least bad choice of all your bad choices – especially if you were hospitalized for something as simple as not being able to afford your insulin.

Is that what happened? No idea. Is that would could have happened? Is our healthcare “system” destroying the lives of hundreds of thousands of WORKING Americans each year a thing? Yes it is.

Run a company that steals millions from their customers with fake fees or signing you up for fake accounts and you get to force your customers into individual binding arbitration if they want it back. Keep a rental car too long and we jump to throwing that person in prison for years.

Also, is the North Carolina law REALLY that keeping a car past the return deadline is a felony? Surely there’s more to it than that? I did that last month when I postponed my flight a day. Hertz added a day to my bill.

Lastly, if this were a random white man, nobody would bat an eye if a rental car company accepted payment of the past-due balance over charging them with a felony. Most of you are only mad because of the picture.

Going from criminal to successful politician. Donald Trump has set the standard that others now follow.

Lock her up!!! Lock her up!!! Lock her up!!!

Borrowing with no intention of ever giving it back? She’s a perfect fit for any Congress!

Republicans have been ripping off the country for at least the last two years and think we’re too dumb to understand. Trump is the swamp personified.

Funny how you constantly criticize Hertz for them filing charges about rental car theft; claiming it’s all fake news. It can never be the dad, working mother, or professional’s fault. Yet when it involves a Democrat, a woman, or person of color then shame on them – they must have stole the car. Not defending the situation, but your reporting is off hard here.

@Realworld – No, the Congresswoman-elect *admits it*

Charlotte is on a political roll. Flying under the radar for now, despite what happened to Iryna Zarutska – victimized by a repeat violent criminal who had no business walking the streets and who has still not been charged for what we all saw. But they are valiantly fighting to not provide any compensation to Zarutska’s family. Thanks to leaders in Chiarlotte that value the lowlifes over the rest of us.

This woman is no exception; someone who actually DID steal a rental car. And yet they elected her to congress. Imagine how corrupt she’ll be given time in DC. Heck, the ones who don’t start out as car theives are corrupt – imagine what a career thief can do!

“Democratic congressional candidate LaKesha”

We have a government headed up by the world’s most successful graft specialist, constantly violating the Constitution and the laws. When there’s a tsunami, the wave brings in a few dubious characters. In this case the status quo was (and is until January) so abominable that a lopsided majority of Americans chose to stop overlooking the malfeasance and incompetence of the ones in charge; and voted for people – not all of them saints – who will replace some of the Members of Congress who have been slobbering all over themselves to be favored pet poodles for the rot at the top.

Just a few decades ago the question was “Is it right or wrong?” Then it became “Is it legal or illegal?”. Now it’s the following sequence: “Is it illegal?”, “Will I be identified?”, “Will I be arrested?”, “Will I be charged?”, “Will I be prosecuted?”, “Will I be convicted?”, “Will the penalty be meaningful?” and “Will the penalty be enforced?”. This doesn’t bode well if we want a functional society.
